# Lifecycle Checklist: ISK-0007 — Container Entry Points & Process Separation

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for start-up, exit codes, liveness, readiness, and the stop sequence are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable
**Created**: 2026-11-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Start-up and Exit Codes

- [x] CHK001 - Is every start-up failure class mapped to exactly one exit code and one error code, with the order in which they are checked? [Completeness, Spec §TR-10, Contract §Command line 2, Data model §State transitions]
- [x] CHK002 - Is it stated that validation and the requirement check complete before any listener binds? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, Contract §Start-up 1, Research R9]
- [x] CHK003 - Is a coordinator selected with no registration mapped to an exit code, distinct from a missing module registration? [Coverage, Hosting contract §Start-up 6.1, Tasks T024]
- [x] CHK004 - Is the refused-mandatory-feature rule defined for all five refusal reasons, and is the release of a held lease on that path stated? [Completeness, Spec §TR-7, §FR-014, Hosting contract §Start-up 7]
- [x] CHK005 - Is the scope of event 7002 consistent between the spec, the contract, research, and tasks? [Conflict, Spec §TR-14, Contract §Diagnostics, Research R4, R9, Tasks T016, T024]
  - Settled in `checklist`: TR-14 named 7002 only for a refused mandatory feature, but research R9 and tasks T016 and T024 write it for every start failure with exit code 2, 3, or 4, and the contract's template carries the error and exit codes. TR-14 and the contract's Diagnostics rule 2 now say 7002 is written for each of those, after the hosting event, and Configuration roots rule 7 names it.
- [x] CHK006 - Are usage errors defined, including that they exit before any configuration is read? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, Contract §Command line 1, 2]

## Liveness and Readiness

- [x] CHK007 - Is liveness's answer and body fixed, and is it stated that it calls no probe or network dependency? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, Contract §Liveness]
- [x] CHK008 - Are all 10 persistence reasons and all 7 coordination reasons mapped, including both forms of `not_configured`? [Completeness, Spec §TR-8, §FR-018, Contract §Readiness 3, 4]
- [x] CHK009 - Is every single-instance state mapped, including `held_by_other`, with its reason code? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, Contract §Readiness 5, Data model §State transitions]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the readiness report's format versioned and fixed, with check order, the `refused` list, and the meaning of `status`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, Contract §Readiness 1]
- [x] CHK011 - Is the response bound of FR-019 achievable as written, given that one evaluation reads two probes? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-019, Contract §Readiness 8, Research R11]
  - Settled in `checklist`: FR-019 bounds the answer by the longest probe's timeout plus its 2-second allowance, which only holds if the probes do not run one after the other. The contract's Readiness rule 8, research R11, and T020 now require them to run concurrently. The 2-second allowance is confirmed in the persistence and coordination contracts' Health rules.
- [x] CHK012 - Is the probe-sharing and caching rule specified, including `readinessCacheDuration` of `0s`, and is US3.4 measurable against it? [Measurability, Spec §US3.4, Contract §Readiness 8]
- [x] CHK013 - Is the readiness-changed event defined, including its first evaluation? [Clarity, Spec §US3.6, Contract §Readiness 9, §Diagnostics 3]
- [x] CHK014 - Is it stated that the traffic listener does not gate on readiness? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011a, Contract §Listeners 6]

## Stop Sequence

- [x] CHK015 - Is the stop sequence ordered, with the delay, drain, reverse stop of start-ups, disposal, events, and exit code? [Completeness, Spec §TR-11, §FR-021, Contract §Lifecycle 1]
- [x] CHK016 - Is it stated how the drain gets `shutdownTimeout` when the host's shutdown timeout also covers the delay? [Clarity, Research R12]
- [x] CHK017 - Is the stop during start-up specified with its readiness answer, events, and exit code, consistently with SC-005? [Consistency, Spec §SC-005, §US2.6, Contract §Lifecycle 2]
  - Settled in `checklist`: SC-005 requires `stopping` at once and exit 0 "including a stop during start-up", but Lifecycle rule 2 named only the wait before disposal. Rule 2, research R12, and T025 now say the lifecycle check turns `stopping` at once with event 7004, and the process writes 7005 and exits 0.
- [x] CHK018 - Are a second signal, an expired `shutdownTimeout`, and a too-short orchestrator grace period each given an outcome? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Lifecycle 3, 4]
- [x] CHK019 - Is the grace-period rule stated with its arithmetic, its default, and the fixture's value that meets it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-021a, Contract §Lifecycle 4, §Test fixtures 2]
- [x] CHK020 - Is it stated that the lease is released only after requests in flight finish, and why the core stops in `StoppedAsync`? [Clarity, Hosting contract §Start-up 8, Research R5]
